name: expiry_seller_v4
first_published: 2026-10-17: the spec-only commit aac2b22 on branch ccr-0cac7edf-61t1mr (pull request 67), pushed 2026-10-17T15:33:49Z, git blob 9fd9088803b472121fe4f5f11f52a650284b77dc; no v4 result or ledger existed. The only edits since are the dates, the forward-start, settlement-treatment and disclosure wording added at the 23 Oct 2026 research review, and the cross-reference to where the rupee figures come from; two rules were added (a verdict hold on a fallback incident, in exit.statistics_and_sources; a v4 pass moves no principle, in reading.consequence) and disclosure figures; no sleeve, strike, threshold or settlement step changed
forward_start: `registered` is the first trading day after the merge to main, and the merge must land before the sleeves' run on that day (if it slips, this date and reading.from are bumped before merging, never after v4 has traded), not the 17 Oct first publication; the first eve this ledger can trade is on or after it; the desk reads it as the floor for eves the sleeves 'did not run' on, so an earlier date would file false skips for eves before v4 existed. The pairing with v1-v3 holds only from the first trade v4 opens. Eves that v1-v3 traded before that have no v4 twin and are excluded from every paired statistic, and the pairing breaks if v4 retires a sleeve that v1-v3 keep opening, or the reverse
kind: forward paper test (no orders): every trade is decided by the rules below before its outcome exists
question: do the five expiry-eve sleeves of expiry_seller_v1, v2 and v3, settled at NSE's official index close instead of the 15:00-15:29 mean of the recorded one-minute closes, stay consistent with their registered benchmark and pay for the real bid/ask? It is the same forward test on the same eves, strikes and fills, with one change: how the settlement price is taken
why: audit finding E-01 (P1). The registered v1-v3 settlement (the mean of the recorded 15:00-15:29 one-minute index closes) is not NSE's official close: against it on 19 recorded days (NIFTY and BANKNIFTY) its mean absolute error was 10.5 bps (NIFTY) and 11.3 bps (BANKNIFTY), at most 35 bps (the audit's figures), while the last one-minute bar equalled the official close on every one of those days (docs/reports/2026-10-04_l1_evidence_audit.md, lines 72 and 317). The desk's index minute series also freezes from about 15:15 to about 15:28 (remediation/HANDOFF_2026-10-16.md, line 131). The sleeve rules (cost check, consistency check, tail rule) run on settled P&L, so a settlement that misses the exchange's own price by that much shifts them by an amount that is the settlement's, not the market's. v4 settles on the official close, which is also the price the options themselves settle on
supersedes: nothing is deleted or edited. From this spec's registration expiry_seller_v1, v2 and v3 (sleeves A to E) keep running unchanged on their own ledgers and settlement rule as comparison ledgers, and v4 is the only ledger that feeds decisions (see `reading`). No v1-v3 trade is imported into, or re-settled by, this spec

reading.decision_ledger: expiry_seller_v4 is the ONLY ledger that feeds eligibility, milestones, principle moves and any allocator
reading.why: F to J enter on the same 15:20 snapshots, strikes and fills as A to E, so the two sets of trades are paired one for one and their cost check and consistency check are the same evidence counted twice (the cost gap is identical trade by trade; only the settlement differs). A to E are therefore comparison-only from this ledger's first trade (see forward_start): no eligibility, milestone, retirement or allocator decision is taken from them, and no principle moves on v4 and v1-v3 cost checks together
reading.cross_ledger_statistic: the per-trade paired settlement gap (v4 settlement against the same eve's v1-v3 settlement, in bps and in rupees per lot): reported, never tested, never a rule
reading.revisit: at v4's 10-trade point on a sleeve and underlying, whether to freeze the matching A to E sleeve (stop opening it) is decided on the record; nothing is frozen by this spec
reading.consequence: a v4 pass moves no principle; a v4 retirement is read as an execution or settlement-plumbing finding, not as evidence about the edge. docs/principles.json still names v1-v3 as the forward tests; read those pointers as the v1-v3 comparison only
reading.disclosure: outcomes of the comparison ledgers before this ledger's first trade are in their own ledgers on the journal branch (3 settled trades each on v1 NIFTY sleeves A and B and on v3 SENSEX sleeves D and E at 22 Oct 2026, below every decision threshold; the 10 official-close side-records so far (6 on NIFTY against NSE's close, 4 on SENSEX against Yahoo's) were 6 lower and 4 higher than the mean-settled P&L: NIFTY in total about Rs 7.1k lower, mostly the 6 Oct eve, SENSEX roughly flat (about Rs 0.1k lower)). Restarting the count here does not remove them: read them beside v4, not instead of it
reading.alarm_gap: once v4 is registered the comparison ledgers raise no sleeve-retired or sleeve-milestone findings. The paired trades settle up to 35-42 bps apart, so a tail breach on a v1-v3 trade may not appear on its v4 twin: it stays visible in the v1-v3 ledgers and in the paired settlement gap, but raises no finding
reading.unverified: the figures in rules.power (expected t after a year, weeks to detect, consistency-check power) come from a research simulation whose script and output are not committed; read them as unverified estimates. A back-of-envelope check from the pooled expiry_eve_law_v2 figures (9.48 bps a week, t 4.98 over 288 weeks, so a weekly sd near 32 bps) gives about 270-340 weeks for 80% power at +4.9 bps and t near 1.1 after 52 weeks, the same order

source.F, G: expiry_seller_v1's per-lot history (sleeves A and B), NIFTY and BANKNIFTY rows: the A0 iron_condor_20_10 and B0 short_strangle_20d rows of docs/prereg/results/expiry_wings_v1-03ed351842ac.md
source.H: expiry_seller_v2's per-lot history (sleeve C), BANKNIFTY: the W5 iron_condor_20_05 row of docs/prereg/results/expiry_wings_v1-03ed351842ac.md
source.I, J: expiry_seller_v3's per-lot history (sleeves D and E): carried from docs/prereg/expiry_seller_v3.json; the rupee figures (mean, sd, worst, p05, win, credit, max_loss_median) are in no committed result file (expiry_eve_law_v1 and v2 report basis points only), so the source of the computation is not in the repo; the figures themselves are identical to the history.per_lot_rupees of expiry_seller_v1, v2 and v3 (F to A, G to B, H to C, I to D, J to E; only the derived t_plain differs), which are their provenance
source.p05: the 5th-percentile column of every sleeve below is carried from expiry_seller_v1, v2 and v3 and is in no committed result file (expiry_wings_v1 reports the 1% and CVaR 5% columns, not p05); nothing in the code reads it
source.official_close_evidence: expiry_eve_law_v2 (spec a3ff6d83a18e), docs/prereg/results/expiry_eve_law_v2-a3ff6d83a18e.md: law L1 with the index level taken from NSE's official closes, in basis points of the index, strangle (short_strangle_20d) and insured (iron_condor_20_05) only

history.convention: the per-lot benchmark of each sleeve is its v1-v3 twin's history, unchanged, so a v4 sleeve is judged against the same numbers (I and J per reference lot, as expiry_seller_v3); evidence class real_eod_approximation. THAT BENCHMARK IS NOT SETTLED ON OFFICIAL CLOSES (and is probably biased low: docs/principles.json records that the old builder's basis error understated the premium, so a consistency pass is weaker evidence than it looks; F has no official-close history anywhere): it was built by the builder that expiry_eve_law_v2 found takes the index level from the nearest future where the bhavcopy has no underlying column (none before 8 Jul 2024, and on weekly expiry days no future expires), which sat +0.19% from NSE's official close on average on 612 weekly expiry days (FINNIFTY +0.26%). The only like-for-like official-close evidence is expiry_eve_law_v2, in basis points and for the strangle and the 20/05 condor only; the 20/10 condor (sleeve F) has no official-close history anywhere. The tests below therefore compare official-close forward P&L with a benchmark whose settlement differs in a way not measured per sleeve
history.caveats: (1) Affected benchmarks: F, G and H (NIFTY and BANKNIFTY, from the nearest-future level) and I and J on FINNIFTY and MIDCPNIFTY (expiry_eve_law_v1 used the same builder and is superseded by expiry_eve_law_v2 as the L1 evidence: n 212/99 against 214/100, MIDCPNIFTY strangle +9.22 bps in v1 against +11.20 in v2). SENSEX's level comes from BSE's file underlying, which the audit matched to Yahoo's ^BSESN on all 142 entry and settlement days. (2) The t values in the earlier specs were not all the studies' own: `t_plain` below is mean / (sd / sqrt(n)) computed from the figures shown, nothing else. (3) as in expiry_seller_v1, v2 and v3: 43 configurations were tried across the earlier studies; FINNIFTY, MIDCPNIFTY and BANKNIFTY moved from weekly to monthly expiries in Nov 2024 (about 12 forward trades a year each); SENSEX history starts in 2024; returns are negatively skewed

pooled_held_out.source: expiry_eve_law_v2, weekly mean across the held-out instruments

official_close_bps.pooled_held_out_text: strangle +9.48 bps a week, t 4.98, 288 weeks; insured +5.48 bps, t 3.63, 288 weeks (expiry_eve_law_v2)

F.risk: defined: expiry_seller_v1's sleeve A, settled at the official close

G.risk: undefined (naked): expiry_seller_v1's sleeve B, settled at the official close

H.risk: defined: expiry_seller_v2's sleeve C, settled at the official close

I.risk: undefined (naked): expiry_seller_v3's sleeve D, settled at the official close

J.risk: defined: expiry_seller_v3's sleeve E, settled at the official close

sleeve_names: new letters after v3's E (F to J, in the order of A to E) so a trade id never repeats an id in the v1-v3 ledgers
size: 1 lot (I, J: 1 reference lot) per sleeve per underlying, as v1-v3; P&L in rupees per lot. Paper only: nothing here places an order or changes the paper account
entry: exactly as expiry_seller_v1, with the holiday and expiry-shift handling it uses (the eve is the session whose next trading day is the underlying's nearest expiry by the holiday calendar, or one the chain tape recorded a chain for): the chain tape's snapshot nearest 15:20 within 15:10-15:25 on the eve, real quotes only, out-of-the-money strikes nearest each delta within 0.08, a two-sided quote on every leg, sells at bid - 0.05, buys at ask + 0.05, statutory fees

exit.rule: held to expiry, cash-settled at the settlement price below; STT on the intrinsic value of exercised long legs at the dated statutory rate the paper broker charges (costs.exercise_stt: 0.15% from 2026-04-01), which this spec names with `exercise_stt: config`. v1-v3 froze 0.125% and keep it
exit.settlement_price: the official index close, from the first of these available under the rules in `when`: (1) NSE's published file (ind_close_all, the value NSE's index options settle on); (2) the 15:29 one-minute close; (3) Yahoo's daily close. The source is recorded with every settlement. The 15:29 link rests on 19 recorded days, NIFTY and BANKNIFTY only, on every one of which the last bar equalled the official close (docs/reports/2026-10-04_l1_evidence_audit.md, lines 72 and 317); it is a fallback, not a proven equivalence. FINNIFTY, MIDCPNIFTY and SENSEX have no recorded minute bars, so they go NSE's file, then Yahoo. SENSEX is a BSE index with no row in NSE's file, so its trades always wait for the next run and then settle on Yahoo's daily close of the BSE index, recorded as such
exit.when: on expiry day (from 15:31) only NSE's published file is accepted. After expiry day the trade falls past NSE's file to the 15:29 close and then Yahoo ONLY when NSE's absence is CONFIRMED: NSE answered with a real HTTP 404 for the file, or the file was fetched and parsed and has no row for that underlying (SENSEX never has one); or after a fixed wait of 2 trading days after expiry (by the holiday calendar) with NSE still not giving a usable answer. Anything else is transient and means the trade waits and the next run asks again: a timeout, a 5xx, a connection error, an unparseable file, and an HTML page served with HTTP 200 in place of the file (it can be a maintenance, WAF or bot-challenge page, so it does not prove the file is missing). With no official close yet the trade stays open: it never falls back to the 15:00-15:29 mean, and the mean is not recorded as a settlement
exit.statistics_and_sources: every settled trade enters its sleeve's cost, consistency and tail statistics whatever its source: the code does not filter by source. The source is recorded on every settlement and the report counts it: NSE's file; the 15:29 bar; Yahoo's close for SENSEX (by design); Yahoo's close or the 15:29 bar on an NSE index (a fallback). A fallback settlement on an NSE index (NIFTY, BANKNIFTY, FINNIFTY, MIDCPNIFTY) is an incident: the desk's self-review files a data finding for it, and a verdict (milestone, eligibility, retirement) on a sleeve that has one in its count is not recorded as a decision until the incident is resolved or the trade is shown to equal NSE's close; a resolved fallback trade stays in the statistics, is never dropped, and the verdict notes it. SENSEX is a BSE index with no row in NSE's file: its settlements are Yahoo's daily close of the BSE index, not an official close. The source is recorded on every settlement (the ledger's settle_source reads 'Yahoo daily close of the BSE index') and counted in the report's sources line ("Yahoo's close (SENSEX, by design)"); the sleeves' rows carry no label, so read I and J on SENSEX as Yahoo-settled. A real HTTP 404 the day after expiry is treated as confirmed absence, so a CDN lag could send a trade to a fallback early; that shows as a fallback incident, not as a clean result
exit.nse_confirmed_absent: a real HTTP 404 for the file, or the file parsed fine and has no row for the underlying (SENSEX always)
exit.nse_transient: no usable answer (timeout, 5xx, connection error, unparseable file, or an HTML page served with HTTP 200): wait; fall past NSE only after nse_wait_trading_days
exit.unsettled: a trade still unsettled after one full session past its expiry is reported as an incident (the desk's self-review files it) and the report counts it at its max loss (defined risk) or at the tail-rule bound, 1.5 x the history's worst (naked), until it settles. That figure is a report line only: it is never added into a sleeve's P&L, its rows, or the tail rule

measured_per_trade: as expiry_seller_v1: P&L, the cost gap against the history's convention at the same snapshot, max loss, margin; plus the settlement source

rules.text: as expiry_seller_v1, on this spec's own settled trades only: the cost check passes when the history's mean plus the 90% lower confidence bound of the mean cost gap stays above zero (z 1.2816), otherwise the sleeve is retired; the consistency check retires a sleeve when (forward mean - history mean) / (history sd / sqrt(n)) < -1.645; a naked sleeve is retired on any single loss beyond 1.5 x the history's worst; a loss beyond a defined-risk sleeve's max loss (exercise STT aside) is a bug, reported as such; a retired sleeve opens nothing more under this spec and does not retire or revive a v1-v3 sleeve. The numbers above are the ones sleeves.py uses; a test pins them to the code

power.source: the research review's simulation (not in a committed file) and the audit's weeks figure

rules.no_profit_claim: the forward record alone cannot show profitability or confirm the edge: the research review puts the expected t after one year at about 0.4 to 1.0 for any sleeve, and the audit puts the weeks needed to detect +4.9 bps a week at about 300 (80% power). The consistency check is a rejection screen, not a confirmation: with the history's own mean and sd the research review's simulation retires about 14.5% of true-edge sleeves by 24 trades, 19.7% by 52 and 24.1% by 104, and at 8 trades it has only about 7% to 18% power to flag a sleeve with zero edge. Monthly naked sleeves (BANKNIFTY, FINNIFTY, MIDCPNIFTY) cannot be eligible before about 13 months (10 trades of the defined-risk sleeve, then 91 days). v4 can therefore really fail only on the cost check, a naked tail breach, or the max-loss bug rule. The simulation figures are the research review's and not in a committed file; the code's rule is not changed here

decision_points: 6 settled trades per sleeve and underlying (cost check), 8 (consistency check), 10 (eligibility), and for a naked sleeve 91 days after its defined-risk sleeve became eligible; the same counts as v1-v3 but counted from this ledger's first trade
eligibility: as expiry_seller_v1 and v3: reported, never applied; the defined-risk sleeve first on each underlying (F on NIFTY and BANKNIFTY, J on FINNIFTY, MIDCPNIFTY and SENSEX), the naked one only after it has been eligible for 3 months; real money only on the owner's word. History restarts: this ledger begins empty and no v1-v3 trade is carried into it, so every count (6, 8, 10 settled trades, the 91 days) starts from zero at this ledger's first trade
retirement: as expiry_seller_v1: cost check failed, consistency rejected, or the naked tail rule breached retires that sleeve on that underlying under this spec only
changes: any change is a new spec with its own ledger; this ledger is never edited
